messages:
kyle: flagging a weird one in the cost dashboard: cache savings migrate across routes when a session crosses billing slabs. saw a customer case where daily rollups moved ~40% of savings between routes. anyone dug into this?

anika: saw that too. root cause seems to be that econ emits per-`billing_window_start` aggregates only, so prefetched tokens in slab X get credited there, but subsequent hits in slab X+1 show up under a different route-hotpath.

rui: are we using fixed minute slabs or sliding windows for the amortization? I remember a convo about moving to sliding.

kyle: currently fixed minute slabs (server groups by `billing_window_start`) - that's why the rollup is non-session aware.

tara: quick repro steps I used: start a session at 23:58, prefetch 2k tokens in slab 23:58-24:00, then hits continue past midnight into slab 00:00-00:10. Dashboard shows prefetch credit in route A (slab A) but hits counted to route B (slab B) and the per-route savings flip in daily aggregates.

rui: we should avoid changing invoice semantics. Proposal: emit an annotation flag on the econ rows like `session_carryover:true` for hit rows that are logically tied to a previous slab. Backend still returns slab totals; UI can present both views.

anika: agree. Minimal backend change. Example payload: `{"slab_start": 169..., "route_id": "r-123", "prefetch": 2000, "hits": 1800, "session_carryover": true}`

kyle: UI idea: two columns "raw_slab" and "session_attributed", plus a toggle "show session-attributed credits". tooltip explaining accounting implications. Tara can mock?

tara: will do a quick mock. also suggest a small "confidence" badge when session attribution is based on sampling heuristics.

rui: performance note: computing carryover requires session-aware grouping which could be heavy for long sessions. Options: (1) compute exact per-session attribution in a streaming aggregator (costly); (2) compute sampled session map (1% sample) and extrapolate; (3) emit carryover only for sessions that explicitly close within the slab boundary.

anika: sampling seems pragmatic. Run a 7-day sim with 0.5% and 1% samples to estimate bias. If error < 0.5% we can ship sampling first.

kyle: SQL for current approach (why it flips):
```sql
SELECT billing_window_start, route_id, SUM(prefetch_tokens) AS prefetch, SUM(hit_tokens) AS hits
FROM econ_prefetch_agg
WHERE billing_window_start >= :start AND billing_window_start < :end
GROUP BY billing_window_start, route_id;
```

rui: sketch of annotated response from the econ API (proto):
```json
{
  "billing_window_start": "2026-03-22T23:58:00Z",
  "route_id": "r-123",
  "prefetch_tokens": 2000,
  "hit_tokens": 1500,
  "session_carryover": true
}
```

tara: UX checklist: explanatory tooltip, toggle, confidence badge, example link to invoice semantics doc. I'll drop Figma link once draft done.

infra-bot: deploy: rolling econ-prefetch-schema migration to staging in ~12m: https://deploys.internal/redwood/8910

kyle: plan of action: (A) anika to add `session_carryover` bool to proto and example payload (PR today); (B) rui to run sampling perf sim and post error margins; (C) tara to mock UI toggle + confidence badge; (D) kyle to run a small end-to-end check on staging after migration. target sync tomorrow 9:30. @anika @rui @tara

anika: opening proto PR now with test payloads.

rui: starting sim, will report numbers in this thread shortly.

tara: Figma mock ETA 3pm PT. :sparkles:

kyle: thanks all. if sampling looks bad we can escalate to building a stream aggregator but let's try sample-first.
